title: Trumpeters Edward Clem, Ned; Wooden Joe's nickname; Lawrence Toca
summary: Glass doesn't remember Clem, explains that Joe Nicholas was nicknamed Wooden Joe for his hard playing, and mentions Toca.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: What about Edward Clem? Did you remember him? No. A trumpet player from uptown.
No, I don't remember Clem. I never worked out with him.
What about the, what's this guy? Babu Augustat that played trombone that Piku talks about?
Babu, I think he called him. He's a old town. I think he was grown when Piku was little.

Yeah. Never know a trumpet player by the name of Ned. I don't know if his last name or first name. Ned, they called him. No. I might know him by her name, you know. I heard that. I heard that. Because you see, all of them had different, they had nicknames. Like we give Wooden Joe, Wooden Joe. He's not Wooden Joe, he's named Joe Nicholas. That's his name, Joe Nicholas. Why'd you call him Wooden Joe? And we called him Wooden Joe, because he played so hard. He never wanted it. When he'd blow that horn, man, he'd throw it up in the air, he'd blow. He was a parade man. And we give him that name Wooden Joe. So he's named Joe Nicholas. Well like Toka played in a lot of parades. Yeah, Lawrence Toka. He was a good little trumpet. He shot himself.
Good blues trumpet player. Yeah, he was good.
